```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

This guide is for work on the client, its generated wrappers and its documentation.
Run development commands from the repository root. A source-package installation
omits `dev/`, `apis/` and the generation configuration, so clone the repository
when you need to change generated code.

## Set up a checkout

The root `.Rprofile` activates renv. Restore the checked-in lockfile before
regenerating the client so that the build uses the pinned specmill release.

```{r restore}
renv::restore()
```

The generation toolchain includes compiled dependencies. The bootstrap script
notes that V8 and yaml12 need a system libv8 and a Rust toolchain when built from
source. Check the installation error for the missing prerequisite before
changing package versions. Ordinary users of echoverse do not need specmill.

Documentation work also needs knitr, rmarkdown, pkgdown and a working Pandoc.
Install missing documentation tools in the development library, then review any
lockfile changes separately from changes to the client.

```{r documentation-tools}
install.packages(c("knitr", "rmarkdown", "pkgdown"))
rmarkdown::pandoc_available()
```

## Put changes in the right place

| Change | Source to edit | Follow-up |
|---|---|---|
| Endpoint names, inputs or selection | `apis/*.yml` | Plan, apply and check generation |
| Published service definition | Downloaded schema in `apis/` | Review the schema diff and generation plan |
| Routes without a published schema | `apis/*.handwritten.swagger.json` | Keep `dev/undocumented-routes.md` consistent |
| Shared Envirofacts request construction | `dev/callbacks.R` and `R/envirofacts_path.R` | Regenerate and run path tests |
| Service errors and retries | `R/echo_response_policy.R` | Regenerate and run response-policy tests |
| Output conversion | `R/envirofacts_tidy.R`, `R/echo_tidy.R` or `R/echo_mapping.R` | Regenerate and run the corresponding tidy tests |
| Envirofacts column types | EPA schema and `dev/build_column_types.R` | Rebuild `inst/extdata/envirofacts-columns.csv` |
| Articles and website navigation | `vignettes/*.Rmd` and `_pkgdown.yml` | Build vignettes and the website |

Wrappers marked `Generated with specmill; do not edit by hand` and their generated
help pages should change through the generation inputs. Client-owned runtime files are fingerprinted by specmill. Applying generation after editing
them updates the recorded state even when wrapper text does not change.

`dev/build_client.R` is a one-time bootstrap and refuses to run while
`DESCRIPTION` exists. Use `dev/regenerate.R` for normal maintenance.

## Regenerate deliberately

Review the plan first. Applying the plan writes generated files; checking it
verifies that the committed output agrees with the inputs.

```{bash regenerate, eval=FALSE}
Rscript dev/regenerate.R plan
Rscript dev/regenerate.R apply
Rscript dev/regenerate.R check
```

When refreshing a published schema, limit the download to the intended API.
The second argument accepts comma-separated API IDs from
`dev/echo_services.csv`. The manifest records source URLs and SHA-256 hashes;
review it with the schema diff.

```{bash refresh-schema, eval=FALSE}
Rscript dev/harvest_schemas.R apis envirofacts
Rscript dev/build_column_types.R .
Rscript dev/regenerate.R plan
```

For a mapping schema refresh, reapply the verified optional-`p_id` fixes and
shared format-hook settings before regeneration:

```{r mapping-configuration}
source("dev/configure_mapping.R")
configure_mapping(".")
```

Downloading a schema does not by itself decide how new routes should be named
or selected. Inspect the corresponding API configuration before applying.
Handwritten schemas are not overwritten by the harvesting script.

## Validate the change

The existing tests exercise response errors, malformed JSON repairs, request
paths and tidy conversion with local data or mocked responses. They do not need
EPA availability. Run the relevant file during development, then the suite.
These examples use testthat's source-directory runner, so no additional test
runner package is needed.

```{r tests}
testthat::test_local(filter = "envirofacts-path")
testthat::test_local()
```

Build the package and check the resulting archive before a release. Substitute
the archive name printed by `R CMD build` if the version has changed.

```{bash package-check, eval=FALSE}
R CMD build .
R CMD check echoverse_0.1.0.tar.gz
```

For documentation changes, build both the installed-package vignettes and the
pkgdown site. Keep live queries in chunks with `eval = FALSE`; package and website
builds should not depend on EPA services or download large datasets.

```{r build-documentation}
rmarkdown::render("vignettes/developer-maintainer.Rmd")
pkgdown::build_site()
```

The repository's R CMD check, commit lint, secret scanning and workflow lint
jobs use pinned reusable workflows from `seanthimons/baseline`. Review the
checks on a pull request as well as local output.

## Diagnose a request or report a problem

Start with the function's help page and a dry run. A dry run constructs an httr2
request without sending it and still validates inputs.

```{r inspect-request}
local({
  old <- options(echoverse.dry_run = TRUE)
  on.exit(options(old))
  request <- echoverse::cwa_get_facilities(p_st = "RI", p_maj = "Y")
  request
})
```

For a live reproduction, reduce the geography and row range first. Session
verbosity reports methods and response statuses. ECHO and Envirofacts service
errors use the `echo_error` class, including error messages returned inside a
successful HTTP response.

```{r diagnose-live}
echoverse::echoverse_run_verbose(TRUE)
tryCatch(
  echoverse::envirofacts_sdwis_water_system(
    "state_code/equals/RI", first = 1, last = 5
  ),
  echo_error = function(error) conditionMessage(error)
)
echoverse::echoverse_run_verbose(FALSE)
```

Open a report in the [GitHub issue tracker](https://github.com/seanthimons/epaechoverse/issues)
with the package version,
`sessionInfo()`, the smallest failing call, the time of the request, the full
error message and the expected result. Include a short response sample when it
helps explain the shape of the data. Review requests and response samples before
sharing them, especially if they include identifiers or credentials added in a
custom session.

Consult the README's known quirks before reporting a missing route. Government-only
`air_viotrack_*` and `ecatt_nif_*` routes cannot be used through EPA's public
service. Some published Envirofacts tables are unavailable, and handwritten
routes can drift from their service implementations.

## Prepare a release

Review generated changes with their input changes, run the generation check and
the offline tests, and build the vignettes and website. Check the package archive
rather than relying only on a source checkout. Update the package version and
user-facing documentation together when names or response behavior change.

A passing offline test suite establishes client behavior against its fixtures.
It does not establish that every upstream route works today. Record any small
live smoke checks separately, including their date and query parameters, so a
service outage is distinguishable from a client regression.
